open_obligations: Check that Smit et al.'s SoM uses the same number of agents and rounds as Du et al.
Note the optional summarisation step in Smit et al.
Check prompts for differences that could explain different results.
in.other_title: Debate protocols compared: Society of Minds and Multi-Persona (angel, devil, judge)
in.rationale: Du et al. define multiagent debate: each agent answers, then repeatedly reads others' answers via a consensus prompt and updates. Smit et al. describe Society of Minds, which they attribute to Du et al. ('Society of Minds (SoM) Du et al. (2023) propose a MAD approach'), as agents giving answers to each other over rounds, optionally summarised, so their SoM description relies on Du et al.'s procedure.
in.scope: proposed DEPENDS_ON: the Society of Minds protocol as Smit et al. describe it

text: The authors define the procedure: each agent (a copy of the same LLM) first answers independently; in each debate round the other agents' responses are concatenated into a consensus prompt and each agent is asked to verify them and update its own response. The round is repeated for several rounds using the updated responses.
title: Multiagent debate procedure: agents read others' answers and update over rounds
